I signed up for a trial yesterday and have been poking around Redwood’s hosted API. I represent an OSS project (Glazy) — our repo: https://github.com/glazy/fast-llm — and we’re exploring how Redwood could fit into our contributor-facing offering (low-cost inference for community-run models).

A few quick things we want to cover in a demo:

- KV caching behavior for multi-tenant small models
- Pricing/credits for open-source projects
- Any prebuilt integrations (K8s/Helm charts, GitHub Actions for CI inference)

Would love to schedule a 30m demo with someone who can speak to both product and integration details. I’m on PST mornings (UTC-8) generally.

Hi Sam — Dev from Redwood’s Solutions team here. Nice to meet you. Short answers up front and a quick pre-demo checklist attached.

Q: Private vs hosted for OSS projects
A: We support both. For community projects where contributors operate model-serving nodes, Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full control; Hosted can be used with strict namespace isolation and token-scoped usage. We have an OSS-friendly credits program we can discuss during the call.

Q: KV caching & multi-tenant small models
A: KV caching is per serving instance; if you want cross-tenant cache benefits we typically recommend a shared serving pool with tag-based routing and prefix-keying. We’ll review batching/latency tradeoffs in the demo.

Q: Integrations
A: We have Helm charts and a reference GitHub Action for model deploys; I’ll bring a short slide + checklist.

Pre-demo checklist (attached): redwood-integration-checklist.pdf — includes sample config snippets I’ll show. If you can paste: 1) expected steady qps per model, 2) model sizes (fp32 / quantized), 3) whether you need on-prem only — that’ll help me tailor the demo.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Re: GitHub Actions for ephemeral CI inference — Dev and I discussed. Short recommendation: use a lightweight eval harness + a local quantized binary for cheap checks, and reserve calls to hosted Redwood endpoints for a small smoke test matrix with very low token budgets. We can provide a token-limited API key and usage quota for CI runs; we’ll cover exact setup in the demo and drop a sample GitHub Action snippet into the shared Drive link below.
